chosen.premise: A sleeping Geodude can be stepped on without waking, then rolls downhill at sunrise looking for food.
chosen.hook: You can step on a sleeping Geodude—and it still won’t wake up.
chosen.visualIdea: Show Geodude half-buried as hikers pass over it, then cut to sunrise and its body rolling downhill.
chosen.note: A remarkably specific contradiction: hikers can step on Geodude while it sleeps, then it rolls downhill for food in the morning. Every beat is directly supported and easy to stage.

candidates.premise: A scholar counted 100 Geodude along one route because they blend into the landscape so well.
candidates.hook: One road had at least 100 Geodude hiding in plain sight.
candidates.visualIdea: A mountain trail fills with rocks, then each one subtly reveals a Geodude face until the counter reaches 100.
candidates.note: The exact count of 100 creates a strong mystery and highly visual reveal. The concealment is supported, though the entry does not explicitly say the scholar counted them because they blended in.

candidates.premise: Geodude climbs steep and even precipitous mountain paths using only its arms.
candidates.hook: Geodude climbs cliffs without using legs—because it doesn’t have any.
candidates.visualIdea: A numbered route traces Geodude gripping handholds up a steep cliff, ending with the full arm-powered climb.
candidates.note: The arm-powered climbing behavior is concrete, distinctive, and repeatedly documented. The hook adds the obvious inference that Geodude has no legs, rather than a fact stated directly in the cited entries.

candidates.premise: Age smooths Geodude’s rocky edges into a round body, but its heart stays hard, craggy, and rough.
candidates.hook: Geodude gets softer-looking with age—but never softer inside.
candidates.visualIdea: Morph a jagged young Geodude into a completely round older one while a glowing rocky heart stays unchanged.
candidates.note: The aging contrast is distinctive and well supported, but the glowing-heart visual is an interpretation, and the entries do not explicitly frame the change as young versus old.

candidates.premise: Mistaking Geodude for a boulder is dangerous: stepping on one can make it swing its fists or chase you.
candidates.hook: That harmless-looking rock might chase you after one careless step.
candidates.visualIdea: A hiker approaches an ordinary boulder, steps on it, and the rock unfolds fists before launching into a chase.
candidates.note: Strongly supported escalation from mistaken boulder to angry fists to pursuit. The general premise is slightly less exclusive because several Pokémon use disguise-based danger.

candidates.premise: The standard 20-kilogram Geodude is Rock/Ground, while its 20.3-kilogram Alolan variety is Rock/Electric.
candidates.hook: Geodude changes one of its types—and gains just 0.3 kilograms.
candidates.visualIdea: Place standard and Alolan Geodude on scales: 20 kg versus 20.3 kg, then swap Ground for Electric.
candidates.note: The 20.0-versus-20.3-kilogram comparison is precise and fully supported, but regional form type changes are a familiar Pokémon angle and the 0.3-kilogram difference is not inherently compelling.

rounds.request: None—sleeping-landmine is strong enough. A stronger alternative would need an equally specific, surprising behavior with a clear visual sequence and direct Pokédex support.
